openQuestions.text: What is the measured setup time of --no-checkout + cp -Rc + index normalization on this APFS host?
openQuestions.note: Reasoned at ~1-4 s from clonefile op counts; needs a prototype measurement to confirm.

openQuestions.text: Which index normalization is correct after manual materialization: clearing skip-worktree bits or seeding the worktree index from the main index?
openQuestions.note: Both are defensible; the index-seed route touches the private worktree gitdir layout and should be pinned by a test.

openQuestions.text: Should the symlinked dep-root write-escape be filed as a containment defect on the shipped design?
openQuestions.note: A lane writing through a linked node_modules mutates the shared install invisibly to both guards; clonefile-ing the roots closes it.

openQuestions.text: Should the missing cumulative churn arm (spec's 40/lane) and the default-3-vs-12 divergence be filed?
openQuestions.note: REQ-004 specifies two arms; the implementation ships one burst check at default 3.

resolvedQuestions.answer: The 22 s / 1.6 GB is git worktree add materializing 82,393 tracked files plus the lane index; the object store was already shared (worktree .git = 4 KB pointer). specs/ alone is 1.3 GB / 78% of tracked files.

Sparse cones and --no-checkout+restore keep exact attribution (private per-lane index; out-of-cone writes still surface as untracked). Shallow/reference/partial clones pay the same materialization and lose worktree semantics — ruled out.

git worktree add --no-checkout + APFS cp -Rc gives a registered lane in ~1-4 s at ~0 disk with exact attribution and a baseline frozen against foreign writes; it also dissolves self-link and entry-guard hazards when dep roots are cloned rather than linked.
resolvedQuestions.source: APFS clonefile semantics over worktree-lifecycle.ts provisioning; worktree-symlinks/synthesis.md

resolvedQuestions.answer: Exact attribution on shared bytes requires kernel mediation: OS write denial (prevention — vacuously exact but changes the question) or observe-by-PID (exact but privileged/entitlement-gated). Tree-diff on shared bytes is structurally unsound by the module's own admission.

Self-links and entry guards are dissolved by a full clone, unchanged under links; the churn detector runs everywhere but is shipped burst-only (spec's cumulative arm absent, default 3 vs 12); symlinked dep roots are a write-escape channel under linking.

git worktree move survives every registered variant (sparse cone, clonefile, full); absolute dep links target the unmoved main checkout; relative self-links were built for relocation. Only enclosing-checkout moves break registrations — a shared constraint.

promotedIdeas.text: Ranked: (a) --no-checkout + APFS clonefile incl. dep roots; (b) sparse-cone worktree as portable fallback; (c) seatbelt-style write denial as optional complement on degraded/shared paths.

pivotsTaken: cost decomposition -> git-native reductions -> filesystem sharing -> single-checkout attribution limits -> relocation matrix
